class.name: BusyChannel
class.description: Busy channel with a relationship to a ResourceBase. Id corresponds to a busy channel number (0-15 for RODBusyModule; 0-2 for LTP, 0-4 for CTPOUT, etc): the channel number where the busy cable is plugged into. The ResourceBase should be the corresponding Resource where the busy is formed. Depending on the Resource, the BusyChannel can be taken into account or ignored. Examples: - ROD for a RODBusy channel - RODBusyModule for a RODBusyModule (the busy that goes out of the RODBusy comes from itself, from the internal OR of its busy channels) - RCDLTPModule for RCDLTPModule (similar to RODBusyModule) - if no resource is available in the database, an ad-hoc Resource can be created. By putting it into the Resources relationship of a segment, one can enable/disable it conveniently.

attribute.name: Id
attribute.description: Id of busy channel: can have different meaning, typically the channel number of the module where this BusyChannel is plugged into.

attribute.name: BusyTimeout
attribute.description: Number of seconds this busy channel is allowed to stay busy at 100%, before its ResourceBase gets automatically disabled. The special case of "0" means that no timeout is used.

attribute.name: RecoveryTimeout
attribute.description: Number of seconds this busy channel is allowed to stay busy before a recovery attempt is performed. The special case of "0" means that no timeout is used.

relationship.name: BusySource
relationship.description: Relationship to the ResourceBase, which provides the busy signal.

class.name: BusyTimeoutAction
class.description: Base class for the action to be performed in caso of a busy timeout or recovery timeout.

class.name: RODBusyModule
class.description: Plugin for ReadoutApplication for the RODBusy VME board. Each busy channel (class BusyChannel) can be linked to the relationship Contains.

attribute.name: TimeoutFraction
attribute.description: Timeout busy fraction threshold: if the busy fraction stays above this threshold, the timeout watchdog will count it as being above threshold.

attribute.name: useConfiguration
attribute.description: Configure the RODBusy according to the oks database

attribute.name: MonitoringLevel
attribute.description: Sets the level of monitoring to be performed on a RODBusy module.

attribute.name: IS_ServerName
attribute.description: IS server name used for RODBusy Monitoring

attribute.name: IS_UpdatePeriod
attribute.description: Period (in seconds) of regular updates for basic and detailed monitoring

attribute.name: ServiceRequest_Limit
attribute.description: Maximum number of counts of the limit counter (100ns intervals of busy, LIMREG register) within the reset period (attribute ServiceRequest_ResetPeriod), at which point a service request is generated.

attribute.name: ServiceRequest_ResetPeriod
attribute.description: Number of 10MHz clock ticks (100ns, IVALREG register) which resets the limit counter.

attribute.name: EmulateVME
attribute.description: For debugging only. If true(=1), all vme access is skipped and the IS entries are filled with mock data. *** NOT YET IMPLEMENTED ***

relationship.name: BusyRecoveryAction
relationship.description: Link to a BusyTimeoutAction plugin which performs user-defined actions when a recovery is requested.

relationship.name: BusyTimeoutAction
relationship.description: Link to a BusyTimeoutAction to be performed when a busy channel has to be removed having hit the large busy timeout.
